name: Vanthorpe OpenFrame Chassis Display Set
description: Architectural cutwork trousers and a structured open-panel vest in matte black technical fabric, designed with deliberate negative space that frames the chassis rather than concealing it. Chrome and alloy components are visible through geometric apertures; internal lighting rigs (sold separately) can illuminate the frame beneath. The fabric panels are rigid enough to hold shape independent of the body wearing them. This is clothing that treats the synthetic form as the main event.
functionality: Rigid panels hold form independent of chassis; optional internal lighting rig mount points built into vest structure.
what_it_says: My chassis is not something I hide — it is something you should appreciate.
story_hooks: The chassis visible through the apertures has unauthorized modifications — someone has been upgrading this unit without registration.
A Spire collector wants to commission the synthetic as a 'living sculpture' for a gala; the offer is insulting and enormous.
related_entities: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Galvanic Resuscitation Frame — 'The Pallbearer's Daughter'

physical_description.visual_profile: A striking architectural statement piece that celebrates rather than hides augmentation. The silhouette is angular and geometric, with deliberate voids creating a skeletal, almost sculptural appearance. When worn by a heavily augmented individual, the chrome and alloy components become the focal point, framed by rigid fabric panels like a museum display case.
physical_description.fit: Exceptionally tailored and structured. The vest and trousers maintain geometric precision independent of body contours. Panels are cut to frame specific chassis components—shoulder joints, spine mounts, femur housings. The fabric architecture creates a compression-like effect without clinging to skin, instead forming a secondary exoskeleton.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte black ballistic weave composite with memory-form ribbing. Panels are rigid enough to hold shape but flex at strategic stress points. Internal reinforcement uses treated synthetic polymer boning.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, technical matte finish with subtle directional ribbing. Up close, the weave is dense and industrial—almost architectural. Panel edges are precisely finished with sealed seams that catch light minimally.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black primary with brushed chrome and dark alloy accents visible through apertures. No prints or patterns—the silhouette and negative space create visual rhythm. Lighting rigs (optional) add cool white or cyan underglow.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap closures along side panels for tool access. The vest uses friction-fit compression tabs at shoulders and waist. Trousers secure with a concealed magnetic retention system at the hips, allowing rapid chassis access.
distinctive_features: Geometric cutout panels precisely sized to frame augmented components
Interior mounting points for optional illumination rigs
Structural panel boning allows self-supporting architecture
Sealed access flaps over sensitive joint areas
Chrome alignment guides etched into fabric edges
Minimal branding—only subtle Vanthorpe mark on interior spine panel
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 luxury augmentation showcase wear. Expensive enough to signal corpo affiliation or wealthy independent; the cost is justified by precision engineering and materials.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by those who've invested heavily in visible chrome and treat their augmentation as identity statement rather than necessary prosthetic. Associated with corpo elites showing off legal enhancements, underground modders flaunting illegal work, or artists treating their body as canvas. Statement: 'Look at what I am. No apology.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new; develops micro-scratches on panels from regular augmentation adjustments and cleaning. High-tier owners maintain immaculate condition. Sub-tier knockoffs show wear quickly at stress points.
